scope: Natural-language routine management through actual Pi; exact chat recipient and draft-preserving entry; Bot profile freshness and intelligent-team member draft retention
skipped: 10 existing opt-in browser/computer-engine checks and 2 Linux-only checks. These engine files were unchanged and this phase did not rerun their previous opt-in results.

behavior.routineManagement: Five scoped actual Pi tools. Source human message, live owner session and Bot/conversation membership are checked per call and again inside mutations. Root/call receipts and mutations are atomic; replay returns immutable prior results, and changed payload or stale configuration revisions fail.
behavior.steering: Accepted same-actor steering immediately invalidates the previous generation. A new generation can authorize mutations only after actual Pi user-message delivery; late assistant turns cannot borrow a newer input. Child, background, manual routine and memory import do not inherit this capability.
behavior.recipient: Explicit Bot is validated against the conversation and persisted separately from automatic routing. Original and retried chat requests must preserve explicit/automatic choice semantics even if both resolve to the same Bot.
behavior.navigation: Existing source chat and Bot are verified under the fixed identity. Existing draft confirmation preserves text, attachments and reply before appending. Busy input or a changed draft/identity cannot be overwritten. No automatic send or task execution.
behavior.settings: Read-only Bot names and roles use the latest source. Switching a planned new Bot to reuse and back preserves its profile and confirmed avatar while retaining the latest assignment.

realModel.note: Bounded synthetic live-model sample, not a guarantee of every natural-language request. Final prompt additionally requests user-facing language rather than internal fields.
